title: React Server Components directives resources and server functions
concepts: React Server Components render ahead of time, before client bundling, in a separate build or request-time server environment. They can access server-side data and keep server-only dependencies out of the client module subtree.
Server Components and Client Components describe execution boundaries, not whether HTML is ever rendered on a server. Client Components can still contribute to server-rendered HTML in frameworks.

The 'use client' directive marks a module boundary; that module and its transitive dependencies belong to the client module subtree. The same component definition can have server-rendered and client-rendered usages depending on the import tree. Add the boundary where interactivity or browser-only capabilities are needed.
Server Components may be asynchronous and await data during rendering. They cannot use client-only state and Effect Hooks; client components handle interactivity.

Server Functions are async server-side functions exposed through a framework or bundler reference. Calling one from client code crosses a network boundary and serializes its arguments and result; React docs recommend using them for mutations, not data fetching.
Server Function arguments are untrusted client input. The server must validate data and authorize every operation; a directive does not provide authentication or authorization.

React documents user-facing Server Components and Server Functions as stable in React 19, while lower-level framework/bundler integration APIs remain unstable across React 19 minor versions. Stability does not remove the need to update vulnerable RSC transport packages; the current security advisories include patched branch versions.

React 19.3 adds support for rendering a Context imported from a 'use client' module directly from a Server Component; React still cannot create Context from a Server Component.
Server Components and Server Functions are documented as stable user-facing features; underlying framework and bundler integration APIs are not semver-stable across React 19 minor versions.
Documentation uses Server Function as the broader term; Server Action refers to a Server Function used as an Action.

A critical RSC transport RCE and a separate high-severity Server Function denial-of-service advisory were published 2026-10-14. Both list the react-server-dom-webpack, react-server-dom-parcel, and react-server-dom-turbopack packages and patched branches 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9, and 19.3.1, but their applicability conditions differ. Resolve framework-bundled versions and update the framework/bundler as directed; do not assume absence of app-defined Server Functions means an RSC-enabled app is unaffected by the RCE advisory.
